root_cause: (a) Milky veil over the woods at clear noon: the volume's clear-haze near thinning (kHazeNearKeep 0.35 at the eye, the full haze only at 2.5 km) gave an optical depth of 0.05 to 0.1 over the first 300 to 600 m. The haze's light is the horizon sky (from the ring), which is 10 to 15 times as bright as a dark conifer wood, so the air made up most of each wood pixel. The debug=8 probe showed about 70% of the left wood's light was in-scatter; fogSun=0 and bloom=0 changed nothing. (b) Two separate smears. On noon_vista, the pale strip down the left edge came from the fog injection weighting the ring by the mean confidence of its nine taps. Azimuths past the screen edge are never seen, so edge columns counted as only about 60% sure and took about 40% of the paler model sky colour. A ring-only probe flattened the edge. On coastline_sunset and every low sun, the flat glow column came from the sky dome's Mie phase: a single broad Cornette-Shanks lobe (g 0.8) that is nearly flat over the first 5 degrees, which the camera's sky roll-off pressed into a column from the sun to the horizon. volFog=0, fogSun=0 and bloom=0 all kept the column; a dome without the Mie term removed it; a two-lobe phase turned it into a glow around the disc.
change_summary: 1) VolumetricFog.hpp: the clear-air near thinning now keeps 0.06 at the eye and reaches the full haze at 3 km. Optical depth falls from 0.08 to 0.015 at 500 m and from 0.18 to 0.05 at 1 km, while 3 km keeps 0.67 (was 0.96) and 5 km keeps 1.57 (was 1.86). Grey sky, rain, fog and dust near air are unchanged. Added the C++ mirror FogHazeNearKeep for tests. 2) EngineGL33_PostFogShaders.cpp injection: the ring weight is now the confidence of the freshest nearby tap (0.1 less per tap from the centre), not the taps' mean. Screen-edge columns use the measured sky; out-of-view azimuths still fade to the model as their measurements age. 3) Mie phase is now 0.7 CS(0.75) + 0.3 HG(0.97), adding the solar aureole's narrow forward peak and still normalised. The change is made in AtmosphereMiePhase (Atmosphere.hpp/.cpp, which the camera's sky integrals also read), in the dome's skyMiePhase and in the sky table row-mean pass's miePhase, so the GPU table and its CPU mirror still agree. Results: the noon_vista woods go from (103,114,126) to (72,82,89) on the left and from (61,72,76) to (43,53,47) on the near right, the far ridges stay pale blue and the left-edge strip is gone. Coastline_sunset's glow now gathers around the sun and fades out radially, with the horizon under it unchanged. Golden hour and dawn glow are kept and slightly more compact around the sun. Other noon views, overcast, rain, blue hour and pine rays show no visible regression.
remaining: The sun's core under the photoreal camera stops at the sky roll-off cap (PhotoCamera kSkyRolloffCap, about 0.85 of white). The glow around the disc is therefore a soft plateau about 2 degrees wide rather than burning white; that constant belongs to the camera and was not touched. Dawn_valley's foreground is darker without the veil (bottom-half luma 94 to 80) but still readable. In noon_vista the camera meters the darker woods and the sky comes out about 8 levels brighter. The ring change was checked on blue_hour_coast, overcast_broken and rain_day but not on night views (the ring is unused at night). The near-haze thinning is still centred on the eye rather than physical; near and far observers agree from about 3 km. root_cause: (a) The gap between the hills is filled by the classic horizon polygon (Landscape::DrawHorizont, from under the horizon up to 0.06 of the far distance, 3.4 degrees) and the dome band under it, drawn in the classic fog colour: warm (193,194,188) under a cool, brighter deck (219,222,229). Probe 1 tinted the band: it is sky depth. With volFog=0 it shows the same warm grey. Its top fade is the hard seam. Under a grey sky the horizon ring sampled just above the land, so it measured this band. The fog volume then converged every far ridge to that colour, which made the flat plate. On top of that, the dry grey-day haze was too thick (grey gain 3.5 left 2% of a ridge at 2 km). Probe 2 (ring sampled above 3.8 degrees, band replaced by the air, fogDensity 0.5) removed the plate and showed the ridges fading in layers. (b) It was not the fog upsample. Turning off the gap closing (probe 2) and a bilateral volume lookup (probe 3) left the rims unchanged. surfAo=0 removed them; surfCanopyAo=0 did not (probe 4). The composite's GTAO and contact shadow darkened whole fogged pixels, because the world's surface shares only hold the classic fog edge. A debug view (probe 5) showed T=0.8 at the trees, so a plain T veil is not enough: the air in front is several times the trees' own light. (c) Rain 0.8 used the full classic-visibility extinction plus grey haze. A hill 300 m away kept about 40% of its contrast and nothing was left past 1 km, while the AI's tactical sight is full to 392 m.
change_summary: Ring shader: under a grey sky it samples from max(first sky + 0.3 deg, 3.8 deg) with 0.6 deg steps, so the air takes the deck's colour above the classic fill. Apply shader: under a grey sky (new fogSkyWeather.z = FogGreySky(skyThrough)) or in rain/fog, sky and far-polygon pixels below the polygon top become the air colour, and the deck above sinks into it over about 5 deg. Before, this was rain/fog only, 0.9 strength, from the horizon line. Medium: grey haze gain 3.5 -> 1.2 (kHazeGreyGain), and rain's weather fog takes kRainFogShare 0.5 of the classic extinction (setFog unchanged). Halo fix: the fog apply writes a second R8 target (FogState::veilTex on the fog FBO's attachment 1) holding the surface's share of the final light, lum(C T)/lum(C T + S). The composite multiplies the surface target's sky and sun shares by it before occlusion and contact shadow, which is exactly occlusion under the fog. It is read on unit 12 (kFogVeilUnit) and unbound after. No new pass. Results: overcast_heavy ridges fade from 1 to 3 km, with no seam (the deck-to-gap column is flat to about 1 level). In rain_day the gap is air continuous with the sky, the 300 m treeline is clear, and the rims and pale skirts are gone at 1080p and at 480 px thumbnails. overcast_broken, town_noon, forest_morning, pine_rays, dawn_valley, town_fog_night and town_night_rain show no regression. root_cause: Both the strip and the pools come from B4 combat light on the ground, drawn by the forward shader's combatLights. The fog, the composite scatter and SSR are not involved. Proof: probe_1 shot one paused frame with each setting. fogLights=0, volFog=0, combatScatter=0 and ssr=0 left the strip and pools unchanged; combatFire=0 removed the fire half of the strip. probe_2 used a tint override: the strip showed green (shell burst) and red (wreck embers, a Fire light), and the rifleman pool showed magenta (the muzzle light, window 3 m or less). Three causes made them so bright at dusk. (1) The combat lights' day scale and flash response used Classic's night effect, which is 1 as soon as the sun is below the horizon. So at 19:35 (sun 1.7 degrees under) fires, bursts and muzzle flashes ran at full night power, while the photoreal camera (CameraNight) still treats that as twilight. (2) The ball wrap (cos + core/d)/(1 + core/d) lit the far plain as if the light stood core metres high, 1.4x to 5x too much at grazing angles. (3) A burst's white-hot flash held 0.15 s at its peak to match Classic's whiteout, even though the flash exposure response is off at dusk.
change_summary: New CombatNight(classicNight, photoCamera, cameraNight). Under the photoreal camera it returns min(Classic's night, the camera's night). It now drives CombatLightSet::Evaluate's day scale (EngineGL33_Lighting.cpp) and FlashExposureGain (EngineGL33_PostCombat.cpp, via CombatState::night). New CombatBallCosine in C++ and combatBallCosine in GLSL (same math). It is the horizon-clipped sphere light (Lagarde and de Rousiers 2014) and replaces the wrap for non-foliage surfaces in combatLights. It gives cos while the ball is above the horizon, (1+cos)/2 at the ball's surface and inside it, and 0 below. New CombatTuning::flashHold (default kExplosionFlashHold). Under the camera it is 0.15 s times the combat night, so at dusk a burst's flash falls from its birth. At full night everything is as before. Results: the muzzle pools are gone at thumbnail and full size. The strip is gone at thumbnail size: the burst band behind the riflemen is gone, and the fire band dropped from 153/132 to 88/80 at column x=800 against a sky of 64. Night re-check: ffh's camp fire and burning Ural light the ground with soft falloff and shadows. In town_night the ground in front of the fire is 2.6 levels darker than with the old wrap on the same build.
remaining: 1) At full size (not at thumbnail size) a faint warm line remains at the horizon near the burning wreck. In the brightest flicker it peaks about 20 levels over the sky, 12 m from the wreck, and is 2-3 px tall. Cause: the rig's dusk ground is metered as dark as a night field. Camera exposure log2 is +2.46 at the dusk firefight (meter mean -9.15), -1.00 at ffh at night (-9.99) and -2.07 in town_night (-4.00). So a fire at the day scale 0.12 reads about as strong at dusk as at night. A knob probe showed combatFire=0.25 puts the line under the sky and 0.1 removes it. Options for the owner: a twilight-based scale for continuous lights under the camera, or a brighter twilight ground fill in the light lane. Not done because it would change the blue hour and daytime look of every continuous light. 2) In its first frame or two at dusk, a shell burst still lights a band of plain about 15 m each side, much dimmer than before. 3) The fire fixer touches nearby code (EngineGL33_Lighting.cpp smoke block, CombatLights.*), so a small merge is likely. 4) In my town_night runs the plume foot is white where the director's final shot shows it orange. root_cause: The landscape draws each terrain square with its own texture. The B7 wet shader (wetSurface) worked out each land pixel's class from that square's albedo, using wetVegetation(albedo) for the grass share and wetGroundPorosity(albedo) for porosity. Both functions are very steep in colour. Two neighbouring squares whose textures differ only slightly in hue (grey gravel patches on one, flat olive on the other) therefore got very different classes. The film (sheen and lamp or sky reflection), the darkening and the puddle threshold all follow that class, so the wet look stopped exactly at the square edge, a straight north-south grid line from the tree base. The B6 SSR trace did the same with the frame colour (grass taken from c0). Probes: the seam stays with ssr=0 and disappears with wetWeather=0. The SSR tag view shows the whole square as terrain, so it is not a road decal. A shader override that wrote out the classes (debug=7: road flag, veg, porosity; debug=2: puddle, damp, film; debug=1: per-draw class) showed veg jumping from mottled 0/1 to a flat 1 at the line, with film and puddles ending there too. The per-draw class was the same on both sides. Strip means of the albedo either side of the line differ by only 2 to 3 levels. Evidence: probe_classes.png, shots_probe1/2.
change_summary: The land's wet class now comes from a continuous world-space field: the land's own colour. TerrainHorizonMap keeps the per-vertex ground colours the builder already received (texture average colours blended over the texture cells around each vertex) as groundColor, with a CPU mirror, SampleGroundColor. The engine uploads it as an RGBA16 texture with a = 1 on unit 12 (kGroundFieldUnit, the slot of the unused kLightDataUnit). The world programs bind it in BindLightingTextures and the SSR trace binds it too. A stand-in with a = 0 is used until the map is built. A new function in the shared Puddles piece, groundFieldAt(xz), reads the field with smoothstep interpolation, so it has no edge and no crease. wetVegetation and wetGroundPorosity moved into that piece, which the forward pass and the trace share. In wetSurface, veg and porosity come from the field; the albedo still darkens per pixel, so texture detail stays. The land no longer pools water as a road because of its texture's name. In the SSR trace, terrain grass comes from wetVegetation(field), so the forward pass and the trace place the same puddles again. In wetPuddle the grass threshold now mixes by veg*veg: the field's veg is an average over mixed ground, and this keeps the puddle share (town_night_rain 0.115 -> 0.134, seam_b 0.039 -> 0.034). The seam is gone at thumbnail and full size in town_night_rain, in four more angles of the square (night and day) and in rain_day, which is otherwise unchanged. The trade-off: mixed ground (the town square) is now evenly wet instead of mottled by the texture's grass and gravel patches.
remaining: For about 0.6 s after an island loads, until the terrain map is built, the land falls back to the per-pixel class, so the old seam can show briefly. A land texture whose name matches a road token no longer pools water as a road (no stock island texture does). The B6 legacy ground path (rain with wetWeather=0) still takes puddle flatness from the per-triangle depth normal; that is not the shipped state. The field is each texture's average colour (GetColor). Cost and motion are not measured; the change adds one more texture read per wet land pixel and per trace texel. Mixed town ground now looks evenly wet rather than mottled; the owner should judge that. Notes: D:/Arma_CWA_worktrees/graphics-remaster/tmp/look/fix/seam/NOTES.md. root_cause: (a) Fire: the combat light on smoke was soft-saturated per channel toward one ceiling and then clipped per channel in the 8-bit decal colour, so strong orange fire light came out white (probe combatSmoke=0: plume foot sat 0.33 vs 0.16 with it on). The round-2 smoke tint tinted the puff's tiny ambient light, not the fire light. The classic flame was the smoke foot lit past white by the classic fire light; the combat light only scatters, so the overhaul had no flame body (camAdditive=2 barely changed the sprite). The cream stone slab was the 0.45 m point-ball fire light several stops past white (combatFire=0 turns them dark). (b) Already fine: shaded ground is dark olive/brown, B lowest everywhere (pine_rays (51,48,35), woods (59,57,38), lowsun (74,66,53), sinai (66,56,45)). (c) The golden warm gain (1.1,1,0.76) was a diagonal gain over the whole frame; on a blue sky it cut blue but not green, turning sky and clouds teal-grey (129,148,163), so the view read as a dull afternoon (probe that undid it on blue light only gave (121,144,176), land unchanged).
change_summary: Fire: new CombatParticleLight keeps the fire light's hue (peak-channel soft saturation, cap 12, tint applied to the added light); Object::DrawDecal keeps the puff colour under 1 by its peak and sends the light past 1 as a new Engine::SetDecalGlow, which EngineGL33::DrawDecal puts in the vertex specular rgb (added by the pre-lit shader path, only under the photoreal camera); new CombatFlameEmission makes puffs within 3 core radii of a fire emit the flame colour (restores the flame body); removed the round-2 3x night smoke boost; under the camera the fire's surface light is deeper orange and comes from a 1.3 m flame body at the same power. Golden hour: the warm gain moved out of the camera colour matrix into a camGolden uniform; the composite applies it by the pixel's warmth (none at (r-b)/peak -0.7, all from 0.4), so blue sky stays blue and land stays golden; the wide ramp avoids an edge round the sunrise glow (a narrow -0.25..0.1 ramp drew one). Shade (b) untouched.
